## Upper-Year Engineering Mathematics {#vol-08 .section-title}

```{=html}
<section class="wh-hero geo-mountains">
  <div class="wh-hero__body">
    <div class="wh-hero__left">
      <p>This is where mathematics stops appearing as a course title and starts appearing as the working language of upper-year engineering. The job is no longer "learn the next theorem" in isolation — it is learning how mathematical structures reappear inside controls, signals, transport, simulation, estimation, reliability, and design.</p>
      <p>You do not need to feel like an "upper-year engineering maths person" to use this volume. If you are a math-curious geographer, an environmental scientist, or a computing student who wants the machinery without the bravado, that is a perfect reason to be here. Every chapter carries a symbol guide and optional domain viewpoints that reveal the same structure in different fields.</p>
```

## Chapter Map {#chapter-map .section-title}

```{=html}
<div class="wh-book-grid wh-reveal">
  <article class="wh-book-card">
    <span class="wh-book-card__status">Ch 1</span>
    <div class="wh-book-card__title"><a href="./01-control-feedback.html">Control, feedback, and stability</a></div>
    <div class="wh-book-card__desc">Turn dynamics into decisions about response and robustness. Transfer functions, root locus, Bode plots — the mathematics of keeping systems on target.</div>
  </article>
  <article class="wh-book-card">
    <span class="wh-book-card__status">Ch 2</span>
    <div class="wh-book-card__title"><a href="./02-discrete-systems-signals.html">Discrete-time systems and signal processing</a></div>
    <div class="wh-book-card__desc">Move from continuous models to sampled systems and filters. The z-transform, difference equations, FIR and IIR filters — the mathematics of digital signals.</div>
  </article>
  <article class="wh-book-card">
    <span class="wh-book-card__status">Ch 3</span>
    <div class="wh-book-card__title"><a href="./03-continuum-transport.html">Continuum mechanics and transport</a></div>
    <div class="wh-book-card__desc">Express materials, fluids, heat, and diffusion as field laws. Stress tensors, Navier-Stokes, advection-diffusion — the PDEs that govern continuous physical media.</div>
  </article>
  <article class="wh-book-card">
    <span class="wh-book-card__status">Ch 4</span>
    <div class="wh-book-card__title"><a href="./04-computational-methods.html">Computational methods for engineering models</a></div>
    <div class="wh-book-card__desc">Turn governing equations into mesh-based computations. Finite difference, finite element, and finite volume methods — discretising continuous problems into solvable systems.</div>
  </article>
  <article class="wh-book-card">
    <span class="wh-book-card__status">Ch 5</span>
    <div class="wh-book-card__title"><a href="./05-estimation-inverse.html">Estimation, inverse problems, and filtering</a></div>
    <div class="wh-book-card__desc">Recover hidden states and parameters from noisy observations. Least squares, Kalman filtering, regularisation — the mathematics of learning what you can't directly measure.</div>
  </article>
  <article class="wh-book-card">
    <span class="wh-book-card__status">Ch 6</span>
    <div class="wh-book-card__title"><a href="./06-reliability-stochastic.html">Reliability, stochastic systems, and quality</a></div>
    <div class="wh-book-card__desc">Model failure, queues, variability, and risk over time. Reliability functions, Markov chains, queuing theory — when the question is not "will it fail?" but "when?"</div>
  </article>
  <article class="wh-book-card">
    <span class="wh-book-card__status">Ch 7</span>
    <div class="wh-book-card__title"><a href="./07-nonlinear-optimisation.html">Nonlinear optimisation for design and operations</a></div>
    <div class="wh-book-card__desc">Choose the best feasible design when tradeoffs are real. KKT conditions, gradient methods, interior-point solvers — optimisation without the luxury of linearity.</div>
  </article>
</div>
```
